chunks: I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a man who has a Jewish or Christian slave-girl and has intercourse with her, and she becomes pregnant. Then he invites her to accept Islam, but she refuses. Her delivery draws near, then she dies while in labor, with the child in her womb, and the child also dies. Should he be buried with her upon Christianity, or should he be taken out from her and buried upon the fiṭrah of Islam? He wrote: “He is buried with her.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: It is not permissible to leave the crucified one on the surface of the earth for more than three days. After that, he is taken down from his wood, and then his corpse is concealed in the soil.

Ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

He was asked about a Christian who is traveling and is with the Muslims, then dies. He said: “A Muslim does not perform ghusl for him, nor any honor; nor does he bury him, nor stand at his grave, even if he were his father.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: Whoever is devoured by a beast, then if some part of him is found containing bone, it is washed, shrouded, perfumed with ḥanūṭ, and buried. If no bone is found in it, it is buried without ghusl as it is found. If what is found of the beast’s prey is his chest or something containing his chest, the funeral prayer is performed over him; but if something other than that is found of him, the prayer is not performed over him. This indicates that.

key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيَّةِ: Christianity; here, the deceased mother’s religious affiliation
key_terms.حُنِّطَ: to be perfumed with funeral camphor or ḥanūṭ
key_terms.صُلِّيَ عَلَيْهِ: the funeral prayer was performed over him
key_terms.فِطْرَةِ الْإِسْلَامِ: the natural disposition of Islam; here, describing the unborn child’s status in the question
key_terms.يُغَسِّلُهُ: to wash him ritually with ghusl for the deceased

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about burying a non-Muslim pregnant woman, a deceased Christian traveler, and partial human remains?
ai.summary: This passage presents legal rulings concerning burial and funerary treatment in several cases: a deceased non-Muslim slave-girl carrying a child from a Muslim man, a Christian who dies while traveling with Muslims, and remains of a person partially devoured by a beast. It also includes a ruling that a crucified body is not to be left exposed for more than three days, reflecting jurisprudential concern with the handling of the dead.
